clue.text: Clothes are covered with no end of fruit

indicators.note: the word are is wrapped by the shortened fruit, so these words mark one piece sitting inside another
no end of tells us to lop the final letter off the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: A remark that garments come smothered in bits of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' leaves APPL; 'covered with' wraps it round the clue's own word 'are', which looks like a mere verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for garments or dress, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Complete directions for entering a right response

indicators.note: the full set of compass points goes into the pair of short pieces, so entering marks an insertion

parts.note: all four compass points, north, south, west and east, abbreviated N, S, W, E

explanation.surface: Full instructions for reaching a correct reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for entering' puts NSWE (all four compass points) between A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or retort to a question is a synonym for this word.

clue.text: Take off staff's wages as extraneous

indicators.note: the staff appears as a foreign body lodged inside the wages, signalling one piece put inside another

parts.note: pay means wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A complaint that staff pay has been docked for being surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as extraneous' pictures the staff lodged as a foreign body. 'Take off' looks like 'deduct', fitting the wages, but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or lampoon them, which is what a spoof or skit does.

clue.text: Whole range runs through to Ireland's housing

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: Ireland's name is shown holding the two short words inside it, so housing marks a container

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
per means through or by way of, as in 'per post'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone whose range stretches all the way to Ireland's homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the container signal, though it reads as homes. 'Whole range' is the definition, not a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's repertoire is the whole range of pieces they can perform.

clue.text: Agreement to let live with freedom from disturbance

parts.note: L is a common abbreviation for live, as on electrical wiring
ease is a state of comfort free from disturbance

explanation.surface: A rental contract that lets the tenant live in peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a legal contract by which property is rented out, an agreement to let.

clue.text: Back for a couple of drinks

parts.note: to sup is to drink, and gives the first of two drinks
port is a fortified wine, the second drink

explanation.surface: Someone backing a friend by buying them two rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to stand behind them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Take place of undressed kid eating cored pears

indicators.note: the leather swallows the trimmed fruit, so eating marks one piece taken inside another

parts.note: suede is kid leather with its surface napped rather than dressed smooth

indicators.note: cored means the centre letter of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: A naked child munching pears with the cores removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cored' drops the middle A to give PERS and 'eating' marks the insertion. 'Undressed kid' looks like a naked child but is suede, leather that is napped rather than dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to replace it, taking its place.

clue.text: Look to make a little noise anyway

indicators.note: anyway hints that the word reads the same in either direction

parts.note: to cheep or squeak faintly

explanation.surface: Glance about, or squeak a little, either will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' says the word works read either way: it is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick look, often secretly.

clue.text: Pass clear water after losing head

parts.note: overt means plain or open, clear to see

indicators.note: the body of water must be taken without its first letter

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Getting by after clear water has lost its source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing head' leaves AKE. 'Clear water' tempts as one phrase; 'clear' is the open-and-plain adjective on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass a vehicle on the road is to go by it from behind.

clue.text: It's raised by country with nitrogen extracted from what the sea leaves

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: it's is read as 'it is', the word it being the piece

indicators.note: N, the chemical symbol for nitrogen, must be taken out

parts.note: Denmark is a country

explanation.surface: A rise in sea level recorded by a nation, seen in its traces on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IT to TI; 'with nitrogen extracted' takes an N out of DENMARK to leave DEMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidemark is the line of debris left on a shore at high water, which the sea leaves behind.

clue.text: 16 sections

annotationWithheld.why: 16 sections (5): STRAP is PARTS reversed, with 16 (BIND OVER) doing both jobs, BIND the definition and OVER the reversal indicator, so one clue word does two jobs.

clue.text: Anxiously await arrest

definitions.meaning: to dread or fear something coming, an older sense of the verb
to seize or take into custody

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to anticipate with fear and to catch and detain a suspect.

clue.text: Chuck senior from tree?

parts.note: elder means senior in age
Chuck Berry was the American rock-and-roll guitarist

explanation.surface: Wondering if a rock musician's father fell from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck senior' looks like a man's father; it is ELDER plus the surname BERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The small dark fruit grows on the elder, so it comes from a tree, with the question mark flagging the loose definition.

clue.text: Dam with a cut in power

indicators.note: the letter A is cut out of the power word

parts.note: steam is a source of power

explanation.surface: A dam built when there was a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cut in' removes A from STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To dam a flow is to stem or check it.

clue.text: Pill-popping city slicker's old foible

indicators.note: the pill is popped open so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: taken as written
EC is the postcode of the City of London
a cad is a slick, dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A drug-taking urban smoothie's former weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popping' means bursting open, so the pill is split to take the rest. 'Slicker' is a smooth operator; 'city' is the London postcode, not a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small fault or weakness, a minor failing.

clue.text: Bloke reduced travelling by bus

indicators.note: the letters travel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man cut down to size by taking the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges BLOKE and REDUCED. 'travelling by bus' looks like the definition is 'travelling'; only 'bus' is.
explanation.definitionFit: A London two-storey bus is called this, so it is a kind of bus.

clue.text: Sparkling fish with an admittedly desirable quality

parts.note: brill is a flatfish

indicators.note: the desirable quality admits, or lets in, the little word

parts.note: 'it' is slang for sex appeal, a desirable quality
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dazzling fish with a quality everyone admits they want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admittedly' means letting in, a container signal. 'It' as sex appeal comes from 1920s slang, the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brilliant sparkles with light, like a gem.

clue.text: Constrain by law to discard port

parts.note: to bin something is to throw it away
Dover is the English Channel port

explanation.surface: Legally forbidding someone to ditch a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine; it is DOVER, the English Channel port.
explanation.definitionFit: A court may bind someone over, ordering them to keep the peace under threat of penalty.

clue.text: Crude oil on tap is not compulsory

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters are put into a rough new order

explanation.surface: Unrefined oil on draught is a matter of choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like it describes the oil; it rearranges OIL ON TAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something optional is left to choice, not required.

clue.text: One initially makes money admitting about chemical in sauce

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of makes
the money lets the other piece in, so admitting marks a container

parts.note: pence are coins, money

indicators.note: about means the chemical is turned around

parts.note: nitre is potassium nitrate, a chemical

explanation.surface: Someone who makes money by putting chemicals in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the chemical to ERTIN; 'admitting' marks the container and 'initially' gives the M. 'Sauce' is the definition, meaning cheek, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is British slang for cheek or insolence, the same idea as rudeness.

clue.text: It's tedious to deal with a complaint

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: Dealing with a complaint is a bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an illness, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Chorea is a nervous disorder causing jerky movement, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Unseemly when chap's bottom is held fast

indicators.note: the last letter is held inside the other word

parts.note: seedy means sordid or disreputable, unseemly

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word's bottom is its last letter

explanation.surface: Something sordid happens when a man's backside is restrained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' takes P from 'chap's'; 'is held' puts it inside SEEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast and speedy are synonyms for quick.

clue.text: Swim across river to get wet

indicators.note: the swim stretches across the river, holding it inside

parts.note: a dip is a short swim

explanation.surface: A dip across the river to get soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts R inside DIP. 'wet' is a noun here, a feeble person.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wet is a feeble, ineffectual person, and so is a drip.

clue.text: Taking on restrictions as retailer did at 6, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a workplace where hiring is restricted to members of one trade union
a shop that shut its doors at closing time, six o'clock for example

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a union-only workplace and, read literally, a store whose doors were shut.

clue.text: Female sailor set up ancient kingdom

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A woman sailor founding an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' gives BA. 'Female sailor' looks like one person; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was an ancient kingdom in southern Arabia, home of the biblical queen.

clue.text: Bread rises with a little help

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the words are written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a tip is a small piece of helpful advice

explanation.surface: Dough rising with a bit of assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns A TIP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat Middle Eastern bread, sometimes spelt this way.

clue.text: 5's point is clear

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
to point is to indicate

explanation.surface: A remark that the fifth point made is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a cross-reference to another answer; it is V, the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame.

clue.text: Integral part is flipping generous

indicators.note: flipping means the run is turned back to front
part means a run of letters taken from within the word

explanation.surface: An essential component that is wonderfully lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' picks EGRAL from 'Integral' and 'flipping' turns it round. 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A large portion is a generous one, a big helping.

clue.text: Name involved in retail banking

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up together

explanation.surface: A named person mixed up in high-street banking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges N with RETAIL. 'banking' looks like finance but means relying, as in 'banking on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banking on something means depending on it, being reliant.

clue.text: Irregular behaviour of creature having nothing for one year

indicators.note: nothing stands for one, so the letter for one is swapped out

parts.note: an animal is a creature
I is the Roman numeral one
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An odd habit of an animal with nothing for a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the I in ANIMAL for O, then Y follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is a deviation from the norm, something irregular.
